recurring_lessons: Ceremony numbers are repo-global, not per-section: ceremonies 2 through 10 (nine consecutive collisions) were each handed an already-closed number and had to renumber themselves from `ls kb/ceremonies/`, since a fix passed as a workflow argument never reaches a run already in flight.

Compose by name, not by copy: a fact a builds_on skill already states must be cited by name plus kb id, never re-derived with new wording; this recurred every wave until enforced as a validate_skills.py warning keyed on (kb id, verbatim quote).

An instruction/invariant/best-practice table overrun is almost always two steps that are one act; every overrun found (wave-1a, wave-2, wave-3c, ceremony-11 groups) was merged without dropping a claim or a citation.

A rule stated in prose but checked by nothing does not stay applied: the fixes that held were the ones turned into a validator warning in the same ceremony that found them (compose-by-name, instruction budgets, version-in-Version-column length, empty references/ directories).

A citation can be a true verbatim substring and still be wrong for the row's claim: the string-match check cannot see that a sentence's subject differs from the row's subject, so a reader has to check the source sentence, not just the quote.
still_open: Many capabilities and guarantees have no adapter/swap-candidate entity in the knowledge base (core components, seam-dispatch, xc-budget, xc-policy-gate, xc-identity-delegation, xc-tenancy, the compose layer), so their -implement skills mint local ids rather than citing one.

The closed problem-type registry (docs/decomposition.md 2.1.6) has no row for several refusal shapes skills now need: a rejected graph edge, an unpriceable plan step, an iteration-ceiling failure, an unwind-failed compensation, an audit-trail integrity break.
Whether xc-tenancy's and cap-isolation's/cap-state-persistence's second-adapter axes are the same swappability proven twice or two genuinely different properties.
No standard's version has been verified against its published specification from this environment; all 552 research records are search-only.
Whether a max_concurrency ceiling per agent profile is enough to keep TARGET T6.6's well-over-a-hundred-concurrent-agent target coherent, or needs a shared resource beyond any one profile.
Whether the ceremony reviewer should be a different agent than the section's author, and whether findings should be scored automatically rather than by one model's judgment.

cap-consumption builds_on agentic-stack alone because it could not name cap-work-intake (wave 3) from a wave-2 position when it was created; the link was left as an open question rather than resolved.
Whose spelling of the closed problem-type registry is normative where docs/skill-manifest.json's fold-in note and docs/decomposition.md disagree (cap-errors).

Whether the restate-and-extend warning's companion limb - one quote per cited id, so no citation is left unanchored - should become a schemas/skill.schema.json requirement; it fires on 608 of 1507 sourced rows (43%) as a check, which is why quality ceremony 01 declined to land it as a gate.
known_defects: Proposed share is near half: 1458 of 2965 rows (49%) across every skill.json carry origin=proposed rather than sourced.
No standard's version has ever been verified against its published spec: all 552 kb/research.jsonl records are status=search-only; live page fetch was blocked in this environment.

The reviewer field on every one of the 13 ceremony records and the plan review is "sonnet" - the same model family grading its own or a sibling instance's output, with no independent or human reviewer.

Ceremony numbering drifted repeatedly: 9 consecutive collisions (ceremonies 2-10) each had to renumber themselves off the directory listing, and ceremony 11 was fanned into three parallel groups (compose, xc, round2) sharing one number instead of three sequential ones.

Consolidation cut the plan from 127 to 99 skills in one same-day, same-session pass (fold 20 of 21 planned -use facets into their ideals; cap-evaluation-use was never authored; drop 4 planned skills) rather than being discovered and corrected incrementally across waves.

2 unresolved instruction-budget warnings remain (cap-agent-runtime and cap-errors at 11 instructions, above the checked 6-10 budget) because no task in scope authorized raising the validator's threshold.

35 compose-by-name restatements remain unfixed (rows repeating a root or sibling fact under an identical quote without naming the owning skill), and the restate-and-extend warning added by quality ceremony 01 opens a further backlog of 204 sourced rows whose post-marker clause is anchored only by the restatement's quote; 5 of those were audited and fixed, the rest are unreviewed.
7 reviewer findings were declined outright (3 in ceremony 9, 4 in ceremony 10) on the reviewer's own say-so, with no independent check on the decision to decline.

Counts in this file and in README.md went stale between the run that wrote them and quality ceremony 01 (build layer 10 vs 11, skills_total 100 vs 101, ledger 22 vs 27, research 541 vs 552); nothing recomputes them, so they are only as fresh as the last hand edit.
